currentFacts: OpenPet is an Electron desktop pet platform with a React Control Center
PetService is the single source of truth for pet state
Control Center owns user-facing configuration

Provider credentials are Shell-owned for persistence; Backend receives an in-memory init copy and sends runtime persistence requests back through the Shell bridge; credentials never enter renderer state, API responses, logs, evidence archives, or ordinary plugin bridges

Current Shell/Backend call chain is main.js -> createOpenPetRuntime() -> createSidecarRuntimeCoordinator() -> spawnSidecar() -> services/backend/index.js; migration remains active and src/main/ is a live Shell boundary

Current executable migration baseline is 87 IPC channels (81 direct registrations, 6 event-only; 41 keep, 31 cutover, 15 blocked), 133 registered REST routes, 146 documented route rows, 21 SSE events, 8 topics, 17 Job kinds, and 6 Job statuses; Settings cursor import and scale preview use strict Backend HTTP routes and a typed Shell reverse bridge while native selection/effects stay Shell-owned; run build:contracts before check:api-contract

2026-10-15 code-only verification: Backend 424/424, Tools 683/683, and changed Settings/AI/Pet Pack regressions 68/68 pass; typecheck, syntax, contracts, API/channel reconciliation, docs drift, and Control Center production build pass; test:core has 26 browser-launch failures because the pinned Playwright Chromium headless shell is absent, and no Electron or desktop UI acceptance was performed

Settings single-writer path is createSettingsStore.patch in Backend plus createSettingsPersistenceQueue in the Shell for FIFO deferred replay; Job cancellation and recovery covers queued/running/finalizing cancellation, duplicate requests, process-tree termination, restart recovery, temp cleanup, and the startup system.jobs-recovered event; the focused Shell reverse-channel slice covers typed plugin production requests, strict ready validation, pending rejection, synchronous-response safety, and graceful shutdown; Task 5 remains partial at native Shell boundaries and compatibility IPC retirement proof
Local HTTP and MCP are loopback-only and disabled by default

The latest fresh-build unsigned macOS arm64 packaged runtime smoke is docs/release-evidence/packaged-runtime/2026-10-09T02-18-20-646Z-darwin-arm64/: 11 of 14 checks pass with isolated user data; three picker-linked checks are pending/blocked because the linked picker report at docs/release-evidence/desktop-picker/2026-10-08T21-01-48Z-darwin-arm64/ predates the HTTP picker cutover and remains 8/9 with plugin-install-disabled pending; a code-level Backend HTTP to Sidecar reverse-channel picker accept/cancel/path-injection smoke passes without desktop UI; public release readiness remains unproven

macOS whole-computer custom cursor scope is backed by a native click-through helper; system scope persists only after activation succeeds, and helper failure or app shutdown restores the native pointer while Windows and Linux remain unsupported
Bundled pets include doro, duodong, and chispa
Codex pet directory import and zip import are supported
Common provider presets such as OpenRouter and Together remain endpoint templates rather than verified integrations; only the OpenPet 8317 gateway preset is tied to archived smoke evidence
Chat provider settings separate active saved config from renderer drafts, support separate save and test connection actions, and avoid the older coupled connection-check workflow
Image generation settings use one OpenAI-compatible image Provider contract with unified OpenAI-compatible provider settings rather than the older split fixture-versus-provider selector model

Creator Studio Pet character generation is governed by docs/pet-character-generation.md: one clean user source, at most one image attachment per Provider request, local composite reference boards, and a required running-right to running-left approved-mirror correction; current orchestration still requests both directional rows independently

OpenPet distribution policy is self-managed signing only: no paid Apple Developer ID/notarization, paid Windows publisher certificate, or third-party signing service; target-OS runtime/install validation and human evidence review remain required

Release workflows and --require-signed closure validators still enforce parts of the previous paid-signing policy and must be adapted to validate ad-hoc/local macOS signatures or locally generated Windows certificates without requiring notarization or publisher trust
Self-signed macOS and Windows packages must not be described as Gatekeeper-approved, notarized, SmartScreen-reputed, or publisher-trusted
Windows target support still needs real installer/runtime smoke evidence under the self-signed policy; paid signing is not a readiness prerequisite
